overview:
Syncthing synchronizes files between two or more computers in real time. This integration allows you to monitor [Syncthing][1] using Datadog.

[1]: https://syncthing.net/
setup:
The Syncthing check is not included in the [Datadog Agent][2] package, so you need to install it.

### Installation

For Agent v7.21+ / v6.21+, follow the instructions below to install the Syncthing check on your host. See [Use Community Integrations][3] to install the Syncthing check with the Docker Agent or earlier versions of the Agent.

1. Run the following command to install the Agent integration:

   ```shell
   datadog-agent integration install -t datadog-syncthing==<INTEGRATION_VERSION>
   ```

2. Configure your integration similar to core [integrations][4].

### Configuration

1. Edit the `syncthing.d/conf.yaml` file in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your [Agent's configuration directory][7] to start collecting your Syncthing [metrics](#metrics). See the [sample syncthing.d/conf.yaml][8] for all available configuration options.

2. [Restart the Agent][9]

### Validation

Run the [Agent's status subcommand][10] and look for `syncthing` under the Checks section.

serviceChecks.name: Can Connect
serviceChecks.description: Returns `CRITICAL` if the Agent can't connect to the Syncthing endpoint, OK otherwise

monitors.title: No active connections
monitors.description: To keep files in sync between different devices a connection needs to be established. This monitor tracks the count of connected deviced. Alerts can indicate a connectivity issue or that the host is not properly synchronizing with others.

monitors.title: Files out of sync
monitors.description: Syncthing ensures that each device has a copy of the synced files. This monitor counts the needed files for each device. Alerts can indicate synchronization issues or that certain files are not properly available on a certain host.

monitors.title: System errors
monitors.description: Errors may occur during the synchronization process due to various issues or problems. This monitor tracks the errors for each device and alerts can indicate a problem during the synchronization process for that host.

monitors.title: Folder errors
monitors.description: Folder errors refer to issues or problems that occur within specific synchronized folders. This monitor tracks the folder errors for each device and folder. Alerts can indicate that errors have occurred within that specific folder.

monitors.title: Service is failed
monitors.description: Syncthing needs to establish and maintain connections between devices or nodes for file synchronization. This monitor evaluates the connectivity status of Syncthing for different hosts to ensure smooth and uninterrupted synchronization of files.

monitors.title: Device is not connected
monitors.description: The Syncthing tool synchronizes files between different devices. This monitor tracks the last seen time, or the last time each device communicated with the Syncthing application, to check that all devices are actively participating in the file synchronization process.
